claims.quote: Our results show significant pathobiological effects and potential mechanisms through which WWOX partial LoF leads to epilepsy, cerebellar neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation, and ataxia.

claims.object_text: mutant knock-in mouse model of Wwox P47T mutation that phenocopies human SCAR12
claims.quote: We generated a mutant knock-in mouse model of Wwox P47T mutation that phenocopies human SCAR12.

claims.object_text: WwoxP47T/P47T mice displayed epilepsy, social and cognition deficits, poor motor coordination, and live beyond 1 year of age
claims.quote: WwoxP47T/P47T mice displayed epilepsy, profound social behavior and cognition deficits, and poor motor coordination, and unlike KO models that survive only for 1 month, live beyond 1 year of age.
WwoxP47T/P47T mice brains revealed signs of progressive neuroinflammation with elevated astro-microgliosis that increased with age.

claims.object_text: reduced molecular and granular layer thickness and reduced number of Purkinje cells with degenerated dendrites (cerebellar degeneration)
claims.quote: Cerebellar cortex displayed significantly reduced molecular and granular layer thickness and a strikingly reduced number of Purkinje cells with degenerated dendrites.

claims.object_text: widespread changes in neuronal and glial pathways and enrichment of bioprocesses related to neuroinflammation
claims.quote: Transcriptome profiling from various brain regions of WW domain LoF mice highlighted widespread changes in neuronal and glial pathways, enrichment of bioprocesses related to neuroinflammation, and severe cerebellar dysfunction.
